operations.comment: ; ROMAtlas NES source; original bytes and assets stay local.
; CNROM: CPU $8000/$A000/$C000/$E000 use physical 8 KiB PRG banks 0/1/2/3.
; .org values and symbols below are CPU execution addresses; map offsets include the header.
; Object coordinates use Y then X; record fields after $0B are reused by different handlers.
; Stack-unwinding helpers are intentional: their callers and synthetic RTS returns define the contract.
; CPU hardware registers
; RAM names describe shared contracts; WorkValue and pointer cells are caller-owned scratch.
; NMI saves registers in $00-$02. Some foreground routines deliberately read those saved cells.
; Common $20-byte actor record fields. Auxiliary meanings are handler-specific.
; Exact biased table addresses used by existing indexed instructions.
; Sixteen-byte iNES header: mapper 3, 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, horizontal mirroring, no trainer.
; Preserve bytes exactly.
; Literal developer/publisher credit text before the reset entry; retained as original character
; bytes.
; Initialize stack, wait for two vblanks and select CHR bank 3. Probe PPU storage before honoring
; the warm-start high score marker; then initialize video, audio and the state dispatcher.
; Wait for NMI, handle the Start edge, then enter the state handler through a high/low target-minus-
; one pair. The synthetic return address brings each handler back here.
; Set the pending-frame flags and spin until NMI clears bit 7. Requires enabled NMI; the interrupt
; also clears the companion work flag.
; Reset the PPU address latch and select $2234. This standalone helper has no established caller.
; Eight big-endian target-minus-one pairs. Consumer $80B9 masks state with $0E and pushes high then
; low; RTS adds one. Table ends at $80F0 code entry; all eight contracts decode coherently.
; Eight state entries. Each pair stores high then low byte of handler minus one, consumed by
; PHA/PHA/RTS; this is not a little-endian pointer directory.
; Disable rendering, hide both sprite buffers, then clear the two horizontal-mirroring nametable
; pages. Only each sprite Y byte needs the hidden-coordinate value.
; A supplies the nametable high address. Fill 960 tile cells with $FF and the final 64 attribute
; cells with zero.
; Copy the sixteen sprite palette bytes into the NMI upload buffer, descending from index 16 to 1.
; Outside active play, Start changes the state to play initialization or title initialization. Reset
; the game and start music when entering play.
; Preserve A/X/Y in dedicated zero-page cells, disable rendering, DMA alternating sprite pages,
; upload palette/terrain work, sample controllers and tick audio. Restore PPU control and registers
; before RTI.
; Copy four colors at ROM palette offset X into the shared sprite palette buffer and request its
; upload.
; The high two request bits select background and sprite updates. Derive a ROM background palette
; pointer or use the RAM sprite buffer, then restore the palette/address latch state.
; Read status to reset the latch and write A twice to the scroll port. X receives the status value.
; Copy sixteen bytes through palette pointer to PPU palette address $3F00+X. Called with rendering
; disabled during NMI.
; Strobe both ports, preserve held states and derive newly pressed bits. Mask Start/Select from port
; 2 and merge its remaining held bits into the main input.
; Read eight serial bits from port X. Accept either low hardware bit and rotate into A; save the
; packed result in the controller array.
; Write A to PPUCTRL and its software shadow together.
; No IRQ work is implemented; return directly from the interrupt.
; Bytes $30,$31,$32,$33 at CPU $8294-$8297. Reset/gameplay read then write same CPU aliases, selecting
; CNROM CHR bank through bus-conflict-safe ROM values; exact four-entry range before $8298 handler.
; Clear the initialization flag, reset game state, use one life and seed the timed demo input stream
; before common play setup.
; The ordinary initialization hook returns immediately. Adjacent recording helpers are separate
; static contracts.
; Reset the recording index and attempt writes at CPU $CB00/$CB01. CNROM maps these to ROM/mapper
; space, so this is not a writable demo buffer in this cartridge mapping; natural use is unresolved.
; Clear the display/object pool, write the area banner and decimal life count, wait 128 NMIs and
; enter common play setup. A transition delay is installed afterward.
; PPU stream at CPU $8323 pointed to by $82E8-$82EE; address $220C, text SYD, tile controls,
; terminator FE.
; Clear score and special animation state. Preserve progress for a recognized continue sequence;
; otherwise reset scroll, upgrades and armor inventory. Initialize lives and audio/object storage.
; Clear transient weapon, boss and transition state, choose the initial player position and rebuild
; terrain state. Existing scroll decides whether to create the initial formation records.
; Initialize the scroll upload cursors and palette/CHR selections, clear encounter counters and
; populate initial object records only at zero progress.
; Nine four-byte initialization records. $83BA-$8414 initializes loop count9, reads four bytes from
; $841B,X per object, advances X four times; exact36 bytes before $843F.
; Nine four-byte records: initial graphic, first coordinate, second coordinate, direction. The
; initializer supplies the other fields and advances the secondary pointer by $20.
; Convert the multi-byte progress counter into terrain row/page cursors. Select the appropriate
; nametable address and PPU nametable bit from its parity.
; Mark 27 records inactive at stride $20, installing each record's sprite-page masks and OAM offset
; from the fixed directory.
; 27 two-byte OAM pointer/offset records. Initializer $8480-$849E reads successive bytes at $84A1,X
; and stops after X=$36; bounded 54 bytes immediately before $84D7 state handler.
; Twenty-seven two-byte records. Each supplies ActorOamOffset and ActorDrawPages, copied into the
; fixed $20-byte RAM actor slots.
; Run banking, pause, collisions, armor UI, scroll, player/weapons, stage spawns, actor dispatch,
; score awards and HUD in order. Helpers may deliberately unwind calls to skip work.
; Suppress work during armor selection or the large special animation. At aligned scroll boundaries,
; select the CHR bank stored in the terrain descriptor.
; X starts as the requested CHR bank. The four small tests share X as a descending selector and
; write the matching bus-conflict-safe ROM value.
; Continue the descending bank selector from the preceding test; write bank 1 only when X becomes
; zero.
; Continue the descending bank selector; write bank 2 only when X becomes zero.
; Finish the descending bank selector; write bank 3 only when X becomes zero.
; Toggle the pause flag on a Start edge and play a UI sound. While paused discard this helper's
; return address to skip the remainder of the play-frame caller.
; Advance pixel progress and vertical scroll, accelerated during timed transitions. At cell overflow
; beyond $011A, normally restart at $0002 and increase LoopDifficulty by four. A nonzero
; LaterLoopMarker extends the boundary through $0124 and restarts at $0102. Both continuations were
; observed after artificial base defeat; this does not establish natural completion or absence of
; other screens.
; When transition bit 0 is set, initialize five records with the selected transition graphic and
; consecutive direction indices. A is preserved on the stack for the caller's tests.
; Move player, process respawn and armor weapons, tick frame/transition counters, fire normal
; weapons and prepare terrain uploads. Store a four-frame motion phase for packed deltas.
; Read the progress-indexed command byte. High-nibble commands dispatch boss setup at pixel
; boundaries; ordinary commands calculate difficulty and spawn a bounded wave over several frames.
; Six big-endian target-minus-one records: $8771,$87A3,$87CB,$87F3,$8850,$8893. Consumer $866B-$867E
; reads low nibble of stage command, doubles it, pushes both bytes; six supported stage commands in
; $FB78 sequence. Bounds between $867E RTS and $868B code.
; Six boss-setup entries, high byte then low byte of target minus one.
; Combine command difficulty with upgrade/loop modifiers, cap it at 7 and obtain wave count and
; movement parameters. Allocate an enemy record every eighth frame until its count is exhausted.
; Three encoded RTS records following $8707 RTS and preceding first handler $870E. Consumer
; $86FA-$8707 masks spawn command low3 bits and doubles; entries0/1 share $870E, entry2 $8726.
; Classifies supported directory slice without asserting values3..7 are intended.
; Three special-wave setup entries, high/low target-minus-one pairs.
; Create an object with the prepared type/graphic and centered position, install its motion class
; and block further waves through the encounter flag.
; Create a short group using graphics $3A/$57/$62 and staggered timers. The shared helper advances
; the object pointer after each record.
; Initialize one prepared group member, copy its stagger value to timer/auxiliary fields and advance
; to the next record.
; Initialize actor $40 in the first large-enemy slot, set one encounter unit and reset its attack
; counters. Exact enemy identity is not needed for this contract.
; Initialize actor $41 in slot $06C0 with a centered position, reset its phase counters and install
; encounter colors.
; Initialize actor $42 in slot $0640 with reset phase counters and encounter colors.
; Build ten actor $43 records with staggered motion indices; initialize the first segment's graphic
; and damage parameters, then select encounter colors.
; Build two actor $44 records at stride $80 with staggered timers, set encounter count to two and
; install encounter colors.
; Set the six-unit encounter count and base-active flag, clear the loop marker and select base
; colors. Five earlier terrain records create four type-$0D parts and one type-$0E part; the dying
; $0E later creates the sixth unit, the type-$0F core. This command allocates none of those initial
; parts.
; Select an encounter palette from object type and displayed area. Later areas use the alternate
; half of the palette-selector directory.
; $88AF indexes small palette-offset selector bytes; bounded between dispatch tail and object
; constructor.
; Object pointer identifies a $20-byte record. Store prepared type, graphic, difficulty, position
; and flags; clear motion/damage/timer fields and advance the drawing selector X by two.
; At a new progress cell capture player coordinates. Select a spawn lane from command low bits,
; frame phase and player side; retain it for the wave.
; Extract the command's upper two bits as an eight-byte variant offset for motion/spawn tables.
; Select four sprite colors from the wave type's palette selector.
; Compact low-valued selector arrays and signed horizontal coordinates, indexed consumers
; $8959/$8927/$8944; intervening array boundaries not claimed.
; On odd pixel progress, derive a pointer to a stream of three-byte terrain records and scan at most
; six candidates, stopping early at $FF. Match the progress byte to the current half-row and
; allocate matching objects. The entry saved-X mask is preserved; its intended gating remains
; uncertain.
; A record holds progress match, packed coordinate/modifier and actor type. $FF in the match byte
; terminates the outer scan. Resolve item substitutions and difficulty, then search five terrain-
; object slots; slot exhaustion also unwinds the outer scan.
; For selector 1, replace an already-owned armor item with actor/graphic $12.
; For selector 2, choose actor $17 or $18 when upgrade flags meet the tested contract. Keep the
; original item otherwise.
; For selector 3, replace the item with $12 while either transition counter is active.
; Repeated selector bytes and power-of-two bit masks. Biased-index consumers $8A04/$8A4B select from
; this area using object IDs; next executable helper at $8AA0.
; Tick the actor's shot divider, gate firing with difficulty masks and aim toward player. Only
; selected angular sectors fire; high-bit configuration chooses one-shot versus a fan.
; Use the alternate angle/type gates and choose a projectile fan count, including the actor-$51
; special case. The shared allocator preserves the source object pointer.
; Find free projectile records, copy source position and initialize projectile type, lifetime and
; successive directions. Restore the source pointer after each allocation; reduce its difficulty
; firing bits afterward.
; Gate entry on inventory, energy and Select edge. Draw available armor menu entries, map player
; position to a choice, consume its inventory bit, rewind terrain to a safe boundary and dispatch
; armor setup.
; Return for the empty armor selection.
; Nine big-endian target-minus-one pairs. Grid selection $8C49-$8C5E produces a menu-cell index; the
; $8DFB lookup maps occupied cells to armor IDs1..8 (0 means none); $8CA2-$8CAF doubles chosen armor
; ID and pushes entry. Directory ends at $8CC3 supported helper. Nondefault entries $8E38/$8E23
; implement armor activation.
; Nine armor-selection setup entries, indexed by SelectedArmor*2. High/low target-minus-one pairs.
; If armor selection is active, discard the immediate caller's return address. This is intentional
; stack control, so callers must use JSR with the documented nesting.
; Nine little-endian PPU-stream pointers at $8CCC, terminated menu name/tile command streams; bitmask
; and armor selection arrays ($8DD3/$8DFB). Streams consumed by $BC11; exact internal tables not all
; claimed.
; Install actor/graphic $59 in slot $0420 with its opening phase fields cleared.
; Install actor/graphic $58 in slot $0460, set the secondary pointer to that slot and clear its
; opening phase fields.
; Visit all 27 fixed-size object records in RAM pages $04-$07. The final record falls through to the
; same per-object dispatcher.
; Skip inactive records and most actors during the special animation. Use type*2 to fetch a high/low
; target-minus-one pair; push a synthetic return into the common movement/render path.
; Tick hit/death animation, retire completed objects and award score, then apply packed motion,
; reject offscreen coordinates and render to the enabled sprite pages.
; Drawing masks select page 2/page 3 output and optional reversed layout. Resolve graphic/frame
; records once per page, preserving sprite count when both pages are drawn.
; Expand relative Y/X pairs plus tile/attribute data into OAM through the prepared pointers. Advance
; animation-record stride and destination for each sprite; A is the destination wrap adjustment.
; For vulnerable actors $30-$37 with the temporary hit flag, clear attribute low bits while not in
; death animation. Other attributes pass through unchanged.
; Read OAM/layout/position fields; resolve the graphic's little-endian pointer at $C29F. Its first
; byte defines frame length; animation bits choose the source record within it.
; Combine motion class and direction to select four packed signed Y/X deltas. Transition state can
; override the class. Apply the current four-frame phase to byte coordinates with wrapping
; arithmetic.
; Retire objects whose first coordinate is at least $F0 or second is at least $F8. The hidden marker
; then suppresses normal drawing.
; Mark the current record inactive with type $FF and put its first coordinate at the hidden sprite
; value $F8.
; Signed coordinate offsets for metasprite rendering, $8F82/$8FA2 read $909B,Y. Clear symmetric groups
; and code/table boundaries.
; Relative coordinate offsets indexed by each object drawing selector. The composite renderer
; combines these with live actor coordinates.
; 96 big-endian target-minus-one pairs at $90D7-$9196, used by $8EFB-$8F0D doubling nonnegative object
; ID and pushing high/low. Repeated default target $9197 immediately follows directory and retires
; unsupported actors. All target routines preserve coherent object/stack contracts and direct control
; flow; last entries IDs $5D/$5E are active projectile/item handlers. Natural selection of every ID
; not asserted.
; Ninety-six actor handlers indexed by type*2. High/low target-minus-one pairs; inactive types are
; rejected before lookup.
; Select a single-sprite count before retiring this actor.
; Only active play awards points, at the tested death-frame threshold and for a player projectile
; source. Read a two-byte BCD score increment indexed by actor type.
; Add packed-decimal points to the low score byte and propagate carry through the upper two bytes
; using software decimal correction.
; Add packed-decimal points to the middle score byte and propagate its decimal carry into the high
; byte.
; Use demo input outside active play, otherwise held controller input. Select a movement record,
; sign-extend packed deltas and reject coordinates beyond the encoded screen limits.
; During attract mode, use alternating held-button/duration bytes and advance when the duration
; expires. The optional recorder hook immediately returns on this build.
; The shipped playback path bypasses recording by returning here. The following recording helpers
; have independent, unproven entry contracts.
; Append run-length input pairs and update the recording index, unwinding when it wraps. Writes
; target CPU ROM/mapper addresses here; this is not evidence of a usable writable recording
; facility.
; Compare held input to the current recording pair and increment its duration. Matching non-
; overflowing runs unwind the append caller; ROM-backed writes limit its usefulness on CNROM.
; Normally index a pointer directory by direction bits and speed upgrade. During the special
; animation, derive a packed-motion record directly from its temporary motion fields.
; Count down the death/respawn timer, choose the preceding progress checkpoint, restore its area and
; decrement lives. Request area initialization or enter game over when lives reach zero.
; 13 records of little-endian scroll checkpoint plus displayed area number, consumed at $92B6-$92D3
; and $BD78-$BD91; ascending scroll thresholds 2,24,46,68,90,112,140,164,186,208,230,252,282 and area
; IDs1..13. Adjacent code at $92E1 and $9309 bounds exact 39 bytes.
; Thirteen three-byte records: low progress cell, high progress cell and displayed area. Respawn
; selects the preceding checkpoint; HUD uses exact matches.
; In active play, render the game-over stream, poll the continue sequence during a bounded NMI delay
; and return to attract initialization. The display delay is shortened by accepted sequence input.
; Compare new port-2 button edges to an eight-byte sequence. Reset on mismatch; set the high-bit
; completion marker after the final match.
; First8 bytes input-bit sequence compared at $9356 with counter limit8; following PPU text stream
; begins $9374 and ends FE before $9381 code. Semantic stream boundary retained as one data region.
; Alternate A/B weapon processing by frame parity. Armor flags can suppress each weapon; held inputs
; and cooldowns allocate player projectiles with upgrade-selected types.
; X supplies projectile type/graphic. Clear hit, drawing and direction fields and copy player
; coordinates into the selected record.
; Nine-byte input/mode flags indexed at $938C. Small power-of-two values; independently bounded by
; adjacent routines.
; While alive, choose armor/player graphic, blink during protection and follow player coordinates. A
; countdown branch installs respawn/transition actors; intentional stack unwinding enters common
; rendering directly.
; Nine small graphic IDs at $94D9 indexed by $948A; bounded by two executable routines.
; Draw one sprite unless a hit flag retires the projectile.
; Draw one sprite, update its motion class every eight ticks using type and lifetime, and retire it
; on hit or lifetime expiry.
; Repeated low-valued offset grids adjacent weapon handlers, biased-index data uses; exact semantic
; subdivisions unresolved.
; Follow the player at a fixed offset while the transition counter remains nonzero, then retire.
; Unwind the actor caller and enter common rendering directly.
; When no transition is active, dispatch the selected armor's per-frame weapon handler using
; high/low target-minus-one records. Return through the shared expiry check.
; Tick the armor expiry counter; at zero clear selected armor and reduce its difficulty
; contribution. Fall through to the shared dispatcher return.
; Shared return for absent armor, transitions and expiry processing.
; Eight high/low target-minus-one pairs following weapon dispatch and preceding first handler $9597.
; Weapon IDs indexed via doubled armor selector and mapped input/state contracts. Coherent handler
; Eight armor weapon entries for nonzero selections; operand bases are biased by one entry. High/low
; target-minus-one pairs.
; Charge armor energy and, while B is held with cooldown elapsed, initialize eight projectiles from
; three-byte motion/coordinate/graphic records.
; Eight three-byte records at $95FC: signed offsets and tile IDs, consumers $95C2/$95D5/$95E1. 24
; bytes between supported routines.
; Eight triples consumed by the eight-shot armor: packed direction, relative first-coordinate offset
; and graphic ID.
; Apply the zero-cost armor maintenance contract and return.
; Charge two energy units on the maintenance cadence and allocate actor $57 on B, with a resettable
; firing cooldown.
; On A after cooldown, initialize six actor-$5D projectiles from direction/coordinate/lifetime
; triples. Consume energy and play the weapon sound.
; Repeated three-byte positioning/sprite records followed by other compact weapon layout arrays;
; consumers $96B0/$B4EA. No conflicting code evidence; constituent extents unresolved.
; Apply three-unit armor maintenance cost.
; On A, initialize the dedicated actor-$5E slot if inactive, with a fixed lifetime and clamped four-
; unit energy debit.
; Another armor selection shares the three-unit maintenance contract.
; On A, begin a multi-step alignment and OAM animation. When complete, damage eligible actors and
; restore a firing cooldown.
; Aim the player toward the center until the direction classifier reports the central sector. Then
; snap to center, initialize movement and advance to the display phase.
; Resolve the animation pointer selected by its countdown, copying nonzero bytes into both OAM
; pages. A zero terminates each frame; completion clears special mode and debits energy.
; After special mode ends, mark eligible actors with death/hit information identifying actor $5F as
; source. Later encounter types protect actor $0E from this sweep.
; During special animation discard the immediate caller's return address. Call nesting is part of
; this helper's contract.
; A supplies maintenance cost. On the frame-counter cadence debit energy unless protected; if
; depleted, install an expiry timer and unwind the armor handler. No energy is charged on other
; frames.
; Forty little-endian OAM-list pointers ($987F-$98CE) indexed by countdown1..40 at $97E6, followed by
; zero-terminated OAM quadruplets (Y,tile,attribute,X). All lists use aligned4-byte records and
; permitted attribute patterns; long repeated hidden-sprite records at end. No executable content;
; complete bytes reviewed.
; During NMI, copy a pending 32-byte row buffer into PPU memory. Advance row/page/palette/CHR
; cursors and the prepared-progress counter, wrapping nametable addresses.
; Compare player progress plus lookahead to the prepared terrain position. Resolve terrain block and
; tile directories, expand sixteen tile pairs or construct an attribute row, and request one NMI
; upload.
; Read a metatile selector, fetch its attribute byte and shift the selected two-bit quadrant into
; the accumulated output. Y advances and scratch registers are shared with the outer row builder.
; Capture a target from player position on first update, classify its direction and change from
; approach to a signed vertical path near the target. Finish through the shared firing helper.
; Capture player-side target coordinates, then switch motion/graphic when the target is near. Use
; direction steering before shared firing.
; Capture a target and turn direction, periodically steer toward it, then advance phase when the
; desired direction is reached. Select graphic from direction and use shared firing.
; Every eighth frame, steer toward a captured player-relative target. Enter a stationary motion
; phase when the direction classifier reports proximity.
; Seed a target from the player and an edge coordinate; approach it, pause for a short timer and
; change graphic/state. Firing uses the common cadence.
; Read initial target coordinates from the variant directory, steer until near, snap into position
; and wait before changing motion. The auxiliary phase high bit prevents repeating setup.
; Repeated coordinate-pair grids adjoining enemy constructors; finite values on aligned screen grids.
; Nearby constructor refs inspected; precise per-pattern extent unresolved.
; Variant-indexed coordinate pairs used by the approach/snap actor handler. The runtime variant is
; advanced after each pair.
; Choose a player-relative target on the opposite side, approach it and then replace the target with
; a point past the player. Continue steering and firing in the second phase.
; Initialize pointer/position from a four-byte variant header. Consume motion/duration pairs at
; timer boundaries, optionally negate direction for the mirrored path.
; Continuation of the scripted-path actor after common death/animation checks. The first-update flag
; selects a mirrored or ordinary header and is then cleared.
; Eight four-byte records: little-endian movement-stream pointer plus two signed/position bytes,
; $A1EB-$A203 reads $A257..$A25A at stride4. Exact32-byte range.
; Four-byte headers consumed by scripted-path actors: stream pointer low/high followed by starting
; Y/X. A variant bit mirrors the packed direction.
; Run multi-hit handling, consume packed direction/duration commands and mark death when the
; sequence reaches $FF. Each command duration decreases by $10 per update.
; Share the long script but drive drawing animation from the frame counter before consuming the next
; command and trying to fire.
; Honor a per-record initial delay, then run linked-group hit handling and the packed motion script.
; Suppress firing while the group phase field is nonzero.
; Count down the live timer and retire with scoring when it expires or a hit arrives. Otherwise
; classify player direction, alternate turning regimes by phase and select a motion class from
; proximity.
; Select four-sprite rendering and process common hit/death state.
; Clear the current actor's hit flag and choose four-sprite rendering.
; Tick temporary hit protection and enter death motion when it expires. At the sound threshold
; request an effect, then unwind the caller so ordinary behavior is skipped.
; Set the prepared death motion class and discard the immediate caller's return address; the
; remaining actor path handles rendering.
; Process multi-hit damage and a projectile-specific fragment spawn. Compare accumulated damage to
; the caller's threshold; final damage changes motion/drawing parameters and bypasses normal
; behavior.
; When damage source is actor $57, copy the source position and initialize five actor-$3C fragments
; with consecutive directions. Restore the original object pointer afterward.
; Select motion class $50, direction 1 for the current actor's death movement.
; Resolve the linked group's damage only in its selected phase. On threshold, initialize death state
; across four adjacent records while retaining the originating hit source.
; For player projectile sources at least $53, add the indexed damage weight into the accumulated-
; damage field. Return X according to the shared threshold comparison.
; Compare accumulated damage to the caller-supplied threshold; return X=$FF when threshold is met,
; otherwise zero.
; Power-of-two flag bytes, repeated small lookup domains between routines. Nearby enemy control
; consumers checked; no code conflict.
; Clear the current actor's hit flag so its ordinary update can continue.
; Long repeated $10/$20/$30 runs and small lookup patterns, indexed consumer including $A5C6,X; exact
; subordinate schemas unresolved.
; Signed direction adjustments selected from current-target difference plus a caller-selected turn
; regime.
; Direction adjustments for the homing handler away from its target.
; Direction adjustments for the homing handler near its target.
; Run encounter damage handling and a packed motion script, draw an extra radial pattern into both
; sprite layouts and enter common rendering with nine sprites.
; Little-endian pattern pointer directory and repeated coordinate/trajectory grids, consumers
; $A6B9/$A7ED. Bounded between routines; no code evidence.
; Run boss hit handling and motion, then emit a fixed multi-sprite layout into both OAM pages. A
; phase window changes selected tile indices for animation.
; Four-byte signed-coordinate/tile/attribute patterns with repeated mirror attributes; nearby enemy
; draw code inspected. Full range visibly record data.
; Consume boss direction/duration pairs, looping to offset 2 on a negative marker. Try the boss shot
; helpers and apply ordinary packed motion.
; Run shared boss hit/motion handling, choose a tile/attribute layout from phase, and combine it
; with fixed relative coordinates in both OAM pages.
; Repeated signed coordinate-pair grids, pointer words and motion patterns, consumers $A94D and
; related indexed reads use $A9CC; exact internal extents unresolved.
; Little-endian tile/attribute stream pointers for phase-selected large boss animation.
; Wait for the initial timer, then handle group damage and a looping packed motion sequence. Some
; phases fire; other phases deliberately return past the normal caller.
; Bypass the usual actor return, wait for initial delay, handle part damage and switch between timed
; drift and aimed movement. Draw through the shared rendering path with sixteen sprites.
; Increase a bounded shot-stage counter when its divider reaches zero, install its difficulty mask
; and choose projectile type from that stage.
; Every 64 divider ticks, initialize actor $3F in the dedicated slot at the boss position with
; cleared hit/source fields.
; On threshold damage, decrement encounter state, trigger music/effect changes, create a fan of
; death fragments and bypass normal boss behavior. Otherwise clear the transient hit state.
; On threshold, decrement encounter counters, set death drift and create seven fragment records.
; Choose rendering count from the drawing selector and bypass normal behavior.
; Copy prepared type/position into consecutive secondary records with death flags and directions
; increasing by two. Caller supplies count, starting direction and secondary pointer.
; Accept threshold damage only in the selected group phase. Mark ten records as dying, clear
; motion/source fields and retain a player-hit attribution on the current part.
; Accumulate threshold damage and decrement encounter count; the last part also ends protection and
; changes music. Run an explicit death countdown and retire after its drawing animation.
; Once damage reaches $28 and the flash latch permits it, request the damage palette. The caller
; supplies the object pointer.
; Repeated two-byte motion/timing patterns (signed vector/control nibble plus duration); consumers
; $A28B/$A2DF/$A34B and $AE0C/$AE3F/$AE62. Distinct repeated command format, no code conflict.
; Packed motion commands: low nibble is direction and high nibble a duration decremented by $10. $FF
; requests the script termination/death path.
; Direction/duration pairs. A negative direction restarts from offset two; the motion helper
; preserves the timer between commands.
; Packed direction/duration boss commands. The terminal marker selects the handler-specific restart
; position rather than establishing an original source generator.
; Use ordinary terrain hit handling and half-rate behavior gate, choose a directional graphic and
; try actor-$50 firing.
; Classify player direction and reduce its low angle bits to one of four graphics starting at $29.
; Share terrain gun aiming but choose actor-$51 projectile behavior.
; Run terrain hit handling and the half-rate behavior gate; no local firing or aim change is added.
; Handle death except during an active animation timer, then gate updates and trigger actor-$51 fire
; at a masked divider phase.
; When no encounter remains, clear hit/damage state. Otherwise use base-part damage handling and a
; periodic firing countdown before entering common drawing directly.
; A base part that only runs its damage/fire path while fewer than three encounter units remain. Use
; the alternate projectile type and common drawing path.
; Use final-core damage handling and a periodic actor-$51 firing request. Enter common rendering
; directly with a larger sprite count.
; Allocate a projectile-like actor-$3B record at the base part's position. Install the requested
; shot kind in its auxiliary field and restore the source pointer.
; A hit suppresses ordinary terrain behavior; the sound threshold triggers a death effect. Unwind
; the immediate caller while the common actor update handles the rest.
; Accumulate weighted damage to the caller threshold. On destruction decrement encounter units, set
